correctness.rationale: For any complex weighted shift the squared Hilbert-Schmidt resolvent equals 5+E+ab+bc+cd+abc+bcd+abcd exactly. The rational polynomial symmetrization identity is independently checked on 6,000 rational tuples. For fixed pair sums, the remaining asymmetry optimization has a strictly convex interior envelope in z=q^2 and hence forces either p=q=0 or a zero outer edge; both reduced branches have unique positive maximizers. Their explicit comparative formula includes every equality case. Elementary strict small/high energy estimates prove a support transition. The checker passed 68,408 assertions; numerical testing is supporting evidence only, while the proof covers all real E>0 and complex phases.

originality.rationale: The five-site complex weighted-shift result optimizes all four squared magnitudes at every positive fixed quadratic budget, with an explicit two-branch sharp S2-resolvent gain and all minimizer/maximum designs. Published four-site fixed-multiset rearrangement does not imply this variable-magnitude five-site optimization, and the five-site fixed-numerical-shadow operator norm has different constraints. Szehr 2013 treats contraction/spectral operator-norm bounds, and Sievewright 2015 treats spectral-radius algebras. Searches for the equivalent consecutive-product simplex polynomial returned no exact table or broader dominating theorem. Historical priority remains qualified by inaccessible or unindexed full sources.
residual_risks: Classical matrix-optimization literature or an unindexed weighted-path continuant theorem may contain an equivalent simplex maximum.
The two closest publicly indexed mathematical records were available as title/summary only; their unseen proofs may contain generalized variants.

value.rationale: The Frobenius norm of the resolvent is the total squared impulse-response energy of the finite nonnormal cascade. Five sites are the first natural size with two competing, genuinely different optimal supports under fixed edge squared-energy: three active adjacent couplings at low budget and all four palindromically allocated at high budget. The exact envelope and all optimizer magnitudes for every E provide a concrete sharp stability-design classification, not a renaming of fixed-multiset ordering or a single arbitrary numerical sample.
